messages:
Meera (PM): Heads up — big customer (fintech) asked for more flexible packaging around caps and bursts. They want a soft monthly token cap (notify + gentle throttle), a paid burst add-on (short-term 2–4x headroom), and explicit contract portability to Dedicated later. Need product + pricing decision this week.
Sam (Sales): They said pain point is unexpected spikes during batch jobs. Willing to pay for burst but insists on clear failover to Dedicated without double-paying.
Lucas (Pricing): Ok — quick thoughts: 1) Soft cap = alerts + 95th-percentile throttles, no hard cutoffs. 2) Burst add-on = prepaid burst units (hours * multiplier).3) Portability fee? maybe credit remaining burst against Dedicated commit. Need numbers.
Owen (Eng-runtime): From infra side soft cap = cheap (alerts + advisory headers). Gentle throttle needs token-bucket change + per-tenant burst accounting. Burst pack implementation will affect autoscaler and admission control.
Kai (SE): Customer example: their nightly ETL creates a 3h spike ~3x baseline. They want predictable cost for that. Suggested product shape: "burst_pack": {"multiplier": 3, "window": "24h", "units": 3 } — buy N units per month.
Anika (Finance): Pricing must be simple. Proposal: base tiers unchanged; add "burst credits" SKU sold in blocks (e.g., 10 credits = x hours at 3x). Credits are refundable as pro-rated conversion if customer moves to Dedicated within contract window.
Dana (Legal): Portability & refund language needs a short clause. Two things: a) non-refundable consumption except if customer transitions to Dedicated within 90 days — then unused credits convert to committed credits with vendor credit applied; b) clear definition of "transition" to avoid gaming. I'll draft.
Lucas (Pricing): Rough numbers so we can test elasticity: sell burst credits at 5x nominal token unit price (because peak inefficiency), with volume discounts. For low-touch launch, keep three SKUs: small (5 credits), medium (20), enterprise (custom).
Meera (PM): Launch criteria proposal: 1) UX for purchasing in Console + API, 2) billing + SKU mapping implemented, 3) runtime throttle behavior validated in staging, 4) legal clause drafted, 5) sample pricing matrix for sales. Thoughts?
Sam (Sales): Need sample talking points and an ROI calc for customers. Without Dedicated portability language some customers won't sign — make Dana's clause high priority.
Owen (Eng-runtime): Technical risk: admission control + quota accounting spans hosted and Dedicated conceptually. For initial launch we can implement burst packs only for Hosted and Dedicated portability is a billing conversion, not runtime migration. That reduces scope but requires clear comms.
Lucas (Pricing): Agreed — ship Hosted-only burst packs for v1. For Dedicated portability offer credit conversion on contract signature, not automated migration.
Kai (SE): Also expose usage telemetry for bursts in Console + webhooks so customers can see when credits are consumed. That reduces disputes.
pricing-bot: New pricing draft uploaded: /pricing/drafts/burst-pack-v1.csv
Anika (Finance): Need to model worst-case margin impact. If we sell bursts cheap customers might exploit. Set floor price and cap per-account burst ratio (e.g., bursts <= 5x monthly baseline unless approved).
Meera (PM): Decision checklist for Thursday: 1) approve Hosted-only v1, 2) SKU + price bands (Lucas), 3) legal portability clause draft (Dana), 4) console + webhook spec (Kai), 5) throttle semantics doc (Owen). I'll run a quick pre-meeting doc.
Sam (Sales): I'll bring 2 pilot customers to sign early if we get portability credit language. Will confirm by EOD.
Dana (Legal): Drafting clause now, will post PR to the contract templates repo tonight.
Owen (Eng-runtime): I'll spike admission control changes and post a short runbook for SRE impact.
Meera (PM): Thanks all — adding short brief to the product board: https://redwood.prod/boards/pricing-burst-pack (WIP). Please drop any blockers here before Thu sync. :slightly_smiling_face:
